title: Amarnath and Vaishno Devi Yatra Suspended as Heavy Rain and Landslides Batter Jammu and Kashmir
excerpt: Authorities halted both pilgrimages after 36 hours of nonstop rainfall damaged routes and triggered landslides, with one woman killed near Baltal. NRIs planning trips should monitor conditions before traveling.
body:
• Both the Amarnath Yatra and Vaishno Devi Yatra have been suspended after 36 hours of continuous heavy rainfall across Jammu and Kashmir.
  • One woman died and three others were injured in a landslide along the Baltal route on July 16.
  • Repair work is underway on both Baltal and Pahalgam routes, with machinery and personnel deployed.
  • The 57-day Amarnath pilgrimage, which began on July 3, is scheduled to conclude on Raksha Bandhan (August 28). About 4.1 lakh devotees have visited so far.

India's two most revered Himalayan pilgrimages — the Amarnath Yatra and the trek to Vaishno Devi — have been suspended after relentless rainfall pounded Jammu and Kashmir for more than 36 hours, damaging routes and triggering landslides that killed at least one pilgrim.

What Happened

Divisional Commissioner of Kashmir Vijay Kumar Bidhuri confirmed the suspension on Thursday, saying both the Baltal and Pahalgam routes leading to the Amarnath cave shrine had sustained significant damage. "Repair work is underway on both routes. With machinery and personnel continuously deployed, resuming the pilgrimage is not currently feasible," Bidhuri said.

The halt came a day after a landslide near Z Morh, between Rayalpathri and Brarimarg along the Baltal route, killed one woman and injured three others. Heavy rain had also blocked pilgrim movement and stranded travelers at multiple points along the yatra corridor.

Vaishno Devi Also Affected

Separately, a landslide struck the Vaishno Devi Yatra route in Katra, Reasi district, injuring four pilgrims. The Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board suspended all yatra-related services, including helicopter operations from Katra to Bhawan and ropeway services from Bhawan to Bhairon Ghati.

The shrine board announced that all bookings during the suspension period will be cancelled with 100% refunds. Devotees can submit cancellation requests to refund@maavaishnodevi.net or contact the call center at 18001807212.

Scale of the Disruption

The 57-day Amarnath Yatra, which commenced on July 3 under what officials called "the most robust security grid in the pilgrimage's history," is scheduled to run until Raksha Bandhan on August 28. About 4.1 lakh devotees have completed the pilgrimage so far this year, trailing last year's pace of 5 lakh by the same point in the season.

Pilgrims can approach the holy cave via two routes: the traditional 48-km Nunwan-Pahalgam track in Anantnag, or the shorter but steeper 14-km Baltal route in Ganderbal district. Both remained closed as of Friday evening.

What NRI Travelers Should Know

The suspension carries particular relevance for diaspora families who plan India trips around the summer pilgrimage season. Thousands of NRIs travel to Jammu and Kashmir annually for darshan at both the Amarnath cave shrine and the Vaishno Devi temple, often booking months in advance.

Authorities have issued weather advisories warning of continued heavy rainfall across the region. The India Meteorological Department has predicted more rain through the weekend, suggesting the suspension could extend further.

For those with upcoming travel plans, officials recommend monitoring updates from the Shri Amarnath Shrine Board (shriamarnathjishrine.com) and the Vaishno Devi Shrine Board (maavaishnodevi.org) before departing. Airlines operating routes to Jammu and Srinagar have not reported cancellations as of Friday, but road conditions remain challenging.

The yatra is expected to resume once weather permits, though officials have not provided a specific timeline.
